evidenceAudit.scope: Endocrine, general and head and neck surgeons, endocrinologists, anaesthetists and primary care doctors in Saudi Arabia preparing an adult for thyroidectomy: history and examination, blood tests, ultrasound and cytology, vocal cord assessment, control of thyroid function, stopping or continuing medicines, consent, and recognising the early complications (bleeding, low calcium, nerve injury) that the pre-operative plan must anticipate. Uses a 2023 Italian society consensus, a Saudi (Bisha) complications study, a hypocalcaemia meta-analysis and product labels. Not for thyroid cancer staging or radioactive iodine planning.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Health Council thyroidectomy guideline was found; the pathway follows the 2023 Italian society (SIUEC) guidance, so waiting-time classes A to D are Italian national priorities and are not Saudi standards.
The American Thyroid Association guideline text could not be opened in full; only the title was found, so its statements are not written.

The SIUEC guidance says beta-adrenergic blockade is recommended in symptomatic thyrotoxicosis and potassium iodide may be given immediately before surgery in Graves disease, but gives no dose; no beta-blocker or potassium iodide regimen is written because no verified dose and no label with a thyrotoxicosis indication was read.

Oral calcium carbonate 2 to 6 g per day in at least three doses is the SIUEC treatment for hypocalcaemia with normal parathyroid hormone, but no calcium carbonate label with this indication was read, so it is described in the steps and not written as a regimen.

Intravenous calcium gluconate is written from the United States label (1000 to 2000 mg as a bolus); the SIUEC example (2 g diluted in 250 mL of normal saline once or twice daily) is quoted in the steps and its concentration (about 8 mg per mL) is a calculation, not a quoted figure.

Calcitriol is written from the United States label for hypoparathyroidism (0.25 mcg once daily in the morning, titrated at 2 to 4 week intervals); SIUEC gives 0.25 to 0.5 mcg once or twice daily; the conflict is flagged for the treating endocrinologist.
Methimazole is written for preparation for thyroidectomy as stated on the United States label; carbimazole, which many Saudi centres use, was not reviewed.
Local thresholds for calcium and parathyroid hormone monitoring after surgery and day-case criteria in Saudi hospitals were not found.
Figures were read by automated extraction of article and label text; spot-check each figure and dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Goitre is common in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia, which has the highest prevalence in the Kingdom (Southwestern Saudi thyroidectomy complications study, Section Introduction). In a series of 339 patients in Bisha, 91.7% had benign and 8.3% malignant disease, and the overall complication rate was 11.3% (Southwestern Saudi thyroidectomy complications study, Section Results). Hypocalcaemia is the most common complication after thyroidectomy, with an overall prevalence of 7% to 51% (Postoperative hypocalcaemia meta-analysis, Section Introduction). Postoperative bleeding with compressive haematoma occurs in 0.1% to 2% and almost always within the first 6 hours (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Prevention and management of complications haemorrhage with compressive hematoma). Twelve risk factors predict postoperative hypocalcaemia, including preoperative vitamin D deficiency (odds ratio 2.32), total thyroidectomy (3.59), hypomagnesaemia (2.85) and thyroid malignancy (1.85) (Postoperative hypocalcaemia meta-analysis, Section Results).

symptoms: Dysphonia, dysphagia or compressive symptoms from the goitre (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).
Symptoms of thyrotoxicosis in hyperthyroidism (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism).
A neck lump or nodule (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Instrumental studies).
Previous neck irradiation or family history of thyroid cancer syndromes (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).
physicalSigns: Thyroid enlargement or nodule on palpation between the cricoid cartilage and the suprasternal notch, and enlarged neck lymph nodes (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).
Ultrasound features suggesting malignancy: hypoechogenicity, micro-calcifications, absent halo, irregular margins (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section First-tier assessments).
Abnormal vocal cord movement on laryngeal assessment (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Pre-admission workup (or upon admission)).
redFlags: Compressive goitre with airway stenosis or severe thyrotoxicosis: priority class A, admission within 30 days (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).
Suspected malignancy: all tumours except small differentiated cancers are class A (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).
Incidental high calcitonin: suspect medullary thyroid carcinoma and measure carcinoembryonic antigen (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Second-tier assessments).
Hypercalcaemia: check parathyroid hormone for primary hyperparathyroidism (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Second-tier assessments).
Anticoagulant or antiplatelet treatment: plan interruption before surgery (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Recommendations for patients).
precipitants: Female sex, 82.6% of the Bisha series (Southwestern Saudi thyroidectomy complications study, Section Abstract).
Residence in a goitre-endemic region (Southwestern Saudi thyroidectomy complications study, Section Introduction).

Graves disease, substernal goitre and recurrent goitre raise the risk of bleeding (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Prevention and management of complications haemorrhage with compressive hematoma).
Preoperative vitamin D deficiency and hypomagnesaemia raise the risk of low calcium (Postoperative hypocalcaemia meta-analysis, Section Results).

clinicalManagement.title: History and examination
actions: Record previous malignancy, neck irradiation, childhood radiation, thyroid cancer syndromes, dysphonia, dysphagia and compressive symptoms (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).
Examine the neck and lymph node chains (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).

Involve a multidisciplinary team of endocrine surgeon, endocrinologist, radiologist and nuclear medicine physician (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Clinical evaluation and pre-operative work up).

clinicalManagement.title: Laboratory and imaging
actions: Measure thyroid stimulating hormone; add free thyroid hormones and antibodies if abnormal; check calcium and phosphorus (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section First-tier assessments).
Perform ultrasound with colour Doppler and fine-needle aspiration cytology as indicated (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Second-tier assessments).
Measure calcitonin before thyroidectomy, and carcinoembryonic antigen if calcitonin is raised (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Second-tier assessments).
Check vitamin D and magnesium to find correctable risk factors for postoperative hypocalcaemia (Postoperative hypocalcaemia meta-analysis, Section Results).

clinicalManagement.title: Control thyroid function
actions: In hyperthyroidism, restore euthyroidism with an antithyroid drug where possible; patients who do not reach it can still be operated safely (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism).

Give a beta-blocker for symptomatic thyrotoxicosis and consider potassium iodide immediately before surgery in Graves disease (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism).

Continue methimazole, propylthiouracil, thyroxine and regular beta-blockers until the day before surgery unless advised otherwise (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Recommendations for patients).

clinicalManagement.title: Pre-admission work-up
actions: Take blood chemistry, full blood count and coagulation tests; record an electrocardiogram; take a chest X-ray if indicated by age and comorbidity (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Pre-admission workup (or upon admission)).
Arrange anaesthesiology consultation and vocal cord assessment (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Pre-admission workup (or upon admission)).
Plan interruption of anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Recommendations for patients).
Prioritise using admission classes A to D (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).

clinicalManagement.title: Consent and preparation
clinicalManagement.timeframe: First visit and day of admission
actions: Explain the indications, alternatives, benefits, complications including nerve injury, low calcium and bleeding, and the consequences of permanent injury; obtain written consent (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Informed consent).
Do not give routine antibiotic prophylaxis; do not pre-deposit blood (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Patient preparation for surgery).
Admit on the day of surgery unless otherwise needed (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Admission).

clinicalManagement.title: Anticipate complications
actions: Check the neck and dressing frequently in the first 24 hours; swelling, restlessness or breathlessness need the surgeon at once (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Prevention and management of complications haemorrhage with compressive hematoma).
Measure calcium (with parathyroid hormone if available) in the first postoperative day; lowest values occur 24 to 72 hours after surgery (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).
Treat hypocalcaemia by severity: oral calcium, add calcitriol if parathyroid hormone is low, intravenous calcium for severe cases (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).
Take levothyroxine one hour before or three hours after calcium (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).

regimens.indication: Control of hyperthyroidism in preparation for thyroidectomy
regimens.patientGroup: Adults with hyperthyroidism listed for thyroidectomy
regimens.dose: Adult initial daily dose 15 mg for mild, 30 to 40 mg for moderately severe and 60 mg for severe hyperthyroidism, divided into 3 doses at 8-hour intervals; maintenance 5 to 15 mg daily (Methimazole label, Dosage and Administration). Dilution and preparation: none; tablets of 5 or 10 mg (Methimazole label, Description). SIUEC advises stopping the antithyroid drug at the time of thyroidectomy (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism).
regimens.frequency: Three divided doses about every 8 hours (Methimazole label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.duration: Until euthyroid and up to the day before or day of surgery as directed by the surgeon and endocrinologist (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism and Section Recommendations for patients)
adjustments: Pregnancy: methimazole can cause fetal harm in the first trimester; consider another agent and use the lowest possible dose (Methimazole label, Warnings).
Liver toxicity and vasculitis are warned about on the label (Methimazole label, Warnings).
Dose reduction of beta-blockers, digitalis and theophylline may be needed when the patient becomes euthyroid (Methimazole label, Drug Interactions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Report fever or sore throat at once; check white cell and differential counts for agranulocytosis (Methimazole label, Warnings).
Prothrombin time before surgery because methimazole may cause hypoprothrombinaemia and bleeding (Methimazole label, Laboratory Tests).
Thyroid stimulating hormone and free thyroxine to avoid hypothyroidism (Methimazole label, Laboratory Tests).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to methimazole or any component (Methimazole label, Contraindications).
regimens.sourceEdition: SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Surgical treatment of hyperthyroidism; Methimazole label, Section Dosage and Administration and Section Indications and Usage

regimens.indication: Hypocalcaemia from postsurgical hypoparathyroidism with low parathyroid hormone
regimens.dose: Initial 0.25 mcg once daily in the morning; increase at 2 to 4 week intervals if response is unsatisfactory; most adults respond to 0.5 to 2 mcg daily (Calcitriol label, Dosage and Administration, Hypoparathyroidism). SIUEC gives 0.25 to 0.5 mcg once or twice daily in addition to oral calcium (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism). Dilution and preparation: none; capsules of 0.25 mcg or 0.5 mcg (Calcitriol label, Dosage and Administration).
regimens.route: Oral, with an adequate daily calcium intake of at least 600 mg from diet or supplement (Calcitriol label, Dosage and Administration)
regimens.frequency: Once daily in the morning (Calcitriol label, Dosage and Administration, Hypoparathyroidism)
regimens.duration: Until parathyroid function recovers (transient if within 6 months) or lifelong if permanent hypoparathyroidism (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism)
adjustments: Check calcium at least twice weekly during titration, then monthly (Calcitriol label, Dosage and Administration).
Withhold other pharmacological vitamin D during treatment (Calcitriol label, Warnings).
Thiazides and digitalis increase the risk of hypercalcaemia or arrhythmia (Calcitriol label, Drug Interactions).
Pregnancy: use only if the benefit justifies the risk (Calcitriol label, Pregnancy).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Serum calcium, phosphorus and 24-hour urinary calcium periodically (Calcitriol label, Laboratory Tests).
Symptoms of hypercalcaemia; stop calcitriol immediately if hypercalcaemia develops (Calcitriol label, Precautions General).
contraindications: Hypercalcaemia or evidence of vitamin D toxicity (Calcitriol label, Contraindications).
Known hypersensitivity to calcitriol or its excipients (Calcitriol label, Contraindications).
regimens.branch: Hypocalcaemia with low parathyroid hormone after thyroidectomy
regimens.sourceEdition: SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism; Calcitriol label, Section Dosage and Administration and Section Contraindications

regimens.patientGroup: Adults with severe or symptomatic hypocalcaemia
regimens.dose: Initial bolus 1000 to 2000 mg of calcium gluconate (10 to 20 mL), repeated every 6 hours if needed, or a continuous infusion starting at 5.4 to 21.5 mg/kg/hour; individualise to symptoms and serum calcium (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.2). SIUEC example: 2 g in 250 mL of normal saline once or twice daily (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism). Dilution and preparation: dilute in 5% dextrose or normal saline before use, to 10 to 50 mg/mL for bolus or 5.8 to 10 mg/mL for continuous infusion; use immediately after preparation (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.1).
regimens.route: Intravenous: slow bolus not faster than 200 mg/minute in adults, or continuous infusion; monitor vital signs and electrocardiogram during administration (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Bolus every 6 hours if needed or continuous infusion adjusted to serum calcium (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.2)
regimens.duration: Until calcium is stable on oral therapy; safety of long-term use has not been established (Calcium gluconate label, Indications and Usage 1)
adjustments: Renal impairment: start at the lowest dose in the range and monitor calcium every 4 hours (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.4).
Avoid with cardiac glycosides; if necessary give slowly with electrocardiogram monitoring (Calcium gluconate label, Warnings and Precautions 5.1).
Do not mix or co-administer with ceftriaxone (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.5).
Measure magnesium and replace if low because magnesium depletion lowers parathyroid hormone action (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Serum calcium every 4 to 6 hours with intermittent doses and every 1 to 4 hours during continuous infusion (Calcium gluconate label, Dosage and Administration 2.3).
Vital signs and electrocardiogram during administration for hypotension, bradycardia and arrhythmia (Calcium gluconate label, Warnings and Precautions 5.4).
Infusion site for extravasation, tissue necrosis and calcinosis cutis (Calcium gluconate label, Warnings and Precautions 5.3).
contraindications: Concomitant ceftriaxone in neonates (28 days or younger) (Calcium gluconate label, Contraindications 4).

regimens.sourceTitle: Calcium gluconate injection: US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism; Calcium gluconate label, Section Dosage and Administration 2.1 and Section Contraindications 4

medicationPlan.note: Medicines tied to the pre-operative and early postoperative plan are written from United States labels: methimazole to control hyperthyroidism before surgery, calcitriol for hypocalcaemia from low parathyroid hormone, and intravenous calcium gluconate for severe or symptomatic hypocalcaemia. Beta-blocker, potassium iodide and oral calcium carbonate are named in the guidance but not written as regimens (see unverified). SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: All tumours except small differentiated cancers limited to the gland; severe thyrotoxicosis; large goitre with significant airway stenosis (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).

Differentiated carcinoma under 1 cm limited to the gland; Tir 3B and large Tir 3A nodules; hyperfunctioning disease with unstable control (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).

Class C within 180 days for hyperfunctioning goitre with good control or growing benign nodules; class D within 12 months for stable large goitre (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Priority for hospital admission).

Calcium below 8 mg/dL with normal parathyroid hormone: oral calcium; low parathyroid hormone: add calcitriol; below 7.0 to 7.5 mg/dL: intravenous calcium (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).

Vitamin K antagonists stopped 3 to 5 days before with low molecular weight heparin bridging; direct oral anticoagulants stopped 24 to 36 hours before; clopidogrel or ticagrelor 5 days, prasugrel 7 days; aspirin not stopped (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Recommendations for patients).
Not indicated except in severe diabetes, cardiac valvular disease or immune deficiency (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Patient preparation for surgery).

patientEducation: We will check your thyroid hormones, calcium, a neck ultrasound and your voice box before surgery.
Take your thyroid tablets until the day before surgery unless we tell you differently.
Tell us about all blood thinners; some must be stopped days before the operation.
After surgery, tell the nurse at once about tingling around the mouth or in the fingers, muscle cramps, swelling of the neck or trouble breathing.
Calcium may be low for a few days or longer; you may need calcium and vitamin D tablets.
lifestyleAndDiet: Follow the instructions about stopping or continuing medicines.
Keep a list of your medicines for the surgical team.
Plan voice rest and follow-up for voice changes.
Take levothyroxine one hour before or three hours after calcium tablets.
mdtReferrals: Endocrine surgeon; endocrinologist; anaesthetist; radiologist; cytopathologist; ear, nose and throat specialist for laryngoscopy; nurse; pharmacist.
dischargeCriteria: Discharge when the neck is dry without swelling, voice and swallowing acceptable, calcium stable, and calcium or levothyroxine instructions given in writing with a follow-up date and warning signs (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hospital discharge and patient information).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Check calcium and parathyroid hormone as directed, thyroid function after levothyroxine start, and pathology review; permanent hypoparathyroidism if not resolved by 6 months (SIUEC thyroid surgery guidance, Section Hypoparathyroidism).
